title: Throughput governor & lookahead cache workshop with Ironclad Finance
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran an Optimize-focused demo exploring a throughput-governor pattern plus lookahead/prefix KV cache tradeoffs for stateful financial chat workloads. Customer cares about 99th p latency, audit logs, and on-prem options. Agreed next steps: run a 48-hour sandbox throughput sim, share SOC2 + KMS docs, and a cost sensitivity spreadsheet tuned to their average session length.
action_items: Marina: produce a sandbox test plan and expected metrics by 2026-09-11
Jasper: send pricing bands and cost sensitivity sheet (worst/median/best) by 2026-09-07
Ethan: share representative session traces and P95/P99 SLO targets by 2026-09-09
next_steps: Schedule 48h sandbox run (Redwood to provision) — target week of Sep 14
Redwood to share SOC2, encryption and KMS integration notes
Follow-up technical deep dive with Priya for VPC/private deployment constraints
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Jasper Cole (Redwood AE); Marina Patel (Redwood SE); Omar Ruiz (Redwood Product); Ethan Ross (Ironclad Head of ML); Priya Menon (Infra); Liam Carter (Platform); Sofia Nguyen (Security)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick optimize/demo on throughput governor + lookahead cache; demoed console sim, cost spreadsheet, and a small live sandbox run plan.

[00:00:00] Jasper: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh welcome. we're going to focus today on two patterns we call the throughput governor and lookahead cache, and show how they interact with KV/prefix cache economics. quick intros?
[00:00:18] Ethan: yeah i'm Ethan, head of ML at Ironclad Finance. primarily interested in chat assistants for customer support, lots of short sessions but occasional long investigations, tail latency is killer for us.
[00:00:33] Marina: thanks Ethan, Priya, Liam — quick note i'm Marina, i'll lead the technical demo. Omar will chime on product constraints.
[00:00:45] Priya: we run mostly on GCP, considering hybrid on-prem for sensitive flows. we care about SSO and KMS integration, and audit trails.
[00:00:58] Jasper: good, noted. quick qualification: what are your typical session lengths and token counts? even rough numbers help the cost sim.
[00:01:10] Liam: median session ~120 tokens, but top 5% go to 3k tokens when a customer walks the transcript. concurrency peaks at end of day ~250 rps.
[00:01:25] Jasper: ok that distribution will shape batching and cache strategies — thanks.
[00:01:40] Marina: jumping in — first concept, throughput governor. it's a routing/limiting layer that prevents individual long sessions from monopolizing batch capacity; it gates requests into fast-path small-batch lanes vs large-batch lanes and can knob toward latency or cost. sketch on screen.
[00:01:58] [screen share sound] Marina: so here on the console you can see per-route governor thresholds, token thresholds, concurrency buckets, and fallback policies.
[00:02:15] Ethan: is governor a new runtime component or config on existing Redwood Dedicated?
[00:02:23] Marina: it's mostly a smart-routing policy in our control plane that maps into runtime placement — doesn't require new model artifacts. for Dedicated and Hosted it's available; for Private we ship the same control-plane hooks but routing runs in the customer's VPC control-plane agent. sometimes the transcript incorrectly calls it "governorized throughput" in our docs, but it's the same feature.
[00:02:45] [00:03:00] Jasper: next, lookahead or 'prefetch' cache — this is targeted caching of predicted future KV cache states for sessionized agents. it pays when you have repeated context or predictable turns.
[00:03:15] Priya: can you explain hit rate expectations? we have fairly diverse dialogues.
[00:03:22] Marina: yes — lookahead is most effective when you have templates or structured flows (forms, repayment flows). we typically see 20-60% prefix hits in those cases; unstructured chats drop lower. the console sim can ingest sample traces to estimate achievable hit rate.
[00:03:40] [00:04:00] Marina: demo: uploaded a small trace sample from a synthetic banking flow — running the Optimize simulator now. you can toggle sessionization strategies: strict session cache, prefix-only, hybrid.
[00:04:18] [sim noise / typing] Marina: running scenario A: median tokens 120, hit rate 28%, batching target 32, gov threshold set to 1.2k tokens. results — estimated token cost drop 38% and 95th latency up ~5ms.
[00:04:45] Ethan: that 38% looks really attractive. what about worst-case when hit-rate collapses?
[00:04:52] Marina: good question — worst-case fallback is to stream to the larger model variant; governor helps cap cost by moving very long chans to a separate lane so short sessions don't see tail inflation. cost sim includes an adversarial trace to show delta.
[00:05:10] [00:05:30] Sofia: security question — are cached KV entries encrypted at rest and do they show up in audit logs?
[00:05:36] Omar: yes, for Private and Dedicated options we support envelope encryption with KMS/HSM. audit logs include cache warm/hits as events; we can emit to your SIEM via syslog or cloud export.
[00:05:58] Sofia: and retention controls? need 7-year for some audit scopes.
[00:06:06] Jasper: retention is configurable per-tenant; we will follow up with a policy doc.
[00:06:20] [00:06:45] Marina: back to economics — here's a sensitivity matrix: x-axis hit rate, y-axis batching size. you can see an island where cost per 1k tokens drops sharply. governor helps you stay in that island by keeping long-running sessions out of the batching pool.
[00:07:05] Liam: operationally, how do we measure when to toggle from prefix to session cache? is that manual?
[00:07:12] Marina: console has a suggestion engine — it looks at live traces and recommends TTLs, prefix lengths, and batch targets. suggestions are just that — you can accept or run a conservative rollout.
[00:07:30] [00:07:55] Ethan: about dedicated vs hosted — for PII-heavy flows we probably need Private. what's the delta in latency and cost? rough numbers fine.
[00:08:05] Jasper: Private has a small latency win for intra-VPC comms but the big cost delta is ops: Dedicated/Private have commitment pricing; hosted is pure usage. we'll send a pricing band but as a rule of thumb, Dedicated commit reduces unit price by ~20-30% at scale.
[00:08:20] Priya: any difference in feature parity for the governor or lookahead cache in Private?
[00:08:27] Marina: feature parity is maintained; some observability exports require additional configuration in air-gapped setups.
[00:08:40] [00:09:00] Marina: demoing a failure scenario: sudden drop in hit rate. console shows a fallback timeline where we automatically widen batching to maintain throughput and trigger a canary model with higher quantization for cost control.
[00:09:21] Ethan: do we need to change our model artifacts for quantization?
[00:09:27] Marina: usually no — Optimize recommends quantization levels and compatible kernels. we do model onboarding to verify and will test in sandbox.
[00:09:45] [00:10:15] Jasper: question from sales: who else on your side will need to be involved for a pilot?
[00:10:21] Ethan: Priya for infra, Sofia for compliance, and one engineer from ML infra to run traces.
[00:10:30] Jasper: perfect.
[00:10:55] [00:11:20] Marina: running a live sandbox sim now — brief run, 10 minutes, scaled to your median/peak.
[00:11:30] [sim run — background hum] Marina: results coming in... median latency 42ms, p95 210ms, p99 480ms with our current governor and prefix settings.
[00:11:58] Priya: p99 480ms is borderline for some flows — can we change the governor to be more aggressive?
[00:12:05] Marina: yes, you tighten the threshold which shifts long sessions to the large-batch lane earlier; that reduces p99 for the fast-path but raises cost slightly.
[00:12:22] [00:12:40] Ethan: tradeoff numbers? one percent change in p99 costs?
[00:12:45] Jasper: i'll share a cost sensitivity table — but ballpark: moving to tighter governor raised unit cost by ~6% in this sim but brought p99 down by 120ms.
[00:13:02] [00:13:30] Marina: also consider session affinity — sticky routing to cache-holding instances raises hit rates but reduces pooling efficiency. the console shows the delta.
[00:13:50] [00:14:10] Liam: do you have recommended default TTLs for financial chat?
[00:14:14] Marina: defaults: short forms 30s-5min TTLs; structured multi-step flows 15-60min; longer investigative sessions you may want session caches with eviction policies tuned by token budget.
[00:14:35] [00:15:00] Sofia: compliance again — is there an on-prem agent that prevents keys from leaving the VPC?
[00:15:07] Omar: yes we ship a VPC agent; keys can be customer-controlled in KMS, we never export raw user transcripts unless explicitly configured.
[00:15:22] [00:15:40] Marina: pivoting to cost model: here's the spreadsheet I uploaded — it models per-token costs, cache hit credits, and amortized GPU cost per batch. you can plug in your traces to see per-route savings.
[00:15:55] [00:16:20] Marina: note an errata: earlier versions of the sheet used "KV hit credit" which sometimes double-counts prefix hits for streaming models — fixed in this copy.
[00:16:36] Ethan: good catch.
[00:16:50] [00:17:10] Marina: demoing a scheduled rollout: suggestion -> canary -> A/B -> full. you can set automatic rollback if quality regressions (BLEU-ish or custom eval) cross threshold.
[00:17:28] Liam: can the console integrate our internal evals?
[00:17:33] Marina: yes, you can upload prompt sets and expected outputs; Optimize will compute regressions and trigger alerts.
[00:17:48] [00:18:10] Jasper: circling back to gating: for a pilot we'd recommend starting with a 10% user sample, conservative lookahead TTLs, and watch hit rate ramp.
[00:18:22] Priya: what instrumentation is required from our side?
[00:18:26] Marina: we need traces with token deltas, session ids, and event markers for session boundaries; SDKs can do this for you.
[00:18:40] [00:19:00] Ethan: can Redwood's optimizer suggest prefix lengths automatically?
[00:19:04] Marina: yes that's part of the suggestion engine — it runs a grid search on prefix length vs TTL vs batch size.
[00:19:18] [00:19:50] Marina: showing example tradeoff: prefix length 40 vs 120 — longer yields higher hit rate but increases cache memory footprint and eviction churn.
[00:20:05] [00:20:30] Sofia: legal will ask about data deletion for individuals. how granular is deletion?
[00:20:36] Jasper: you can purge by session id or time range; Private gives you direct access to storage so deletion is auditable. we'll provide a deletion playbook.
[00:20:55] [00:21:15] Marina: simulating a weekend load — batching goes up, hit rate stays stable, cost curve flattens for batch sizes above 64.
[00:21:30] Ethan: how sensitive is this to model size changes? if we drop to a smaller open model does the economics shift?
[00:21:40] Marina: yes, smaller models reduce per-token cost but may increase latency; Optimize recommends quantization and batch size combos per model. we also track model variants in the console.
[00:21:58] [00:22:20] Priya: any hidden operational costs we should budget for?
[00:22:26] Jasper: include storage for KV cache, network egress if cross-region, and monitoring retention. we'll itemize these.
[00:22:45] [00:23:10] Marina: quick Q&A: Eli? (note: speaker label mismatch sometimes shows Speaker 1)
[00:23:16] Speaker 1: uh thanks, i guess — how long to run the sandbox to get meaningful stats?
[00:23:22] Marina: 48 hours with representative traffic is ideal; you can start with 4-6 hour smoke runs.
[00:23:35] [00:24:00] Jasper: time check — final section: operationalizing the pilot. we'll provision a sandbox, run the sims, and come back with a tuning session.
[00:24:12] Ethan: sounds good. next, specific asks: can you include a breakdown of the effect on p95/p99 vs unit cost?
[00:24:20] Jasper: yes — that's in the next steps.
[00:24:45] [00:25:05] Marina: last note: competitors often offer static caching layers; our differentiator is runtime-aware prefetch plus governor routing which keeps short sessions fast while capturing prefix wins.
[00:25:22] Liam: are there any tradeoffs for multi-tenant setups?
[00:25:29] Marina: multi-tenant adds isolation overhead and you might prefer per-tenant TTL profiles; we can model that.
[00:25:50] [00:26:10] Jasper: wrap-up — we'll send the sandbox plan, SOC2 + KMS docs, cost sheet, and schedule the infra deep dive. thanks all.
[00:26:25] Ethan: thanks everyone.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Transcript has a few speaker label glitches; some lines show "Speaker 1".
- Agreed pilot scope is sandbox sim + 48-hour run if sample traces look representative.
